body:
## Why

Decapod #1628 needs an instance-scoped local/cloud connector and typed managed authentication/account transport. Existing adapter selection alone does not provide this lifecycle.

## Changes

- Recover connector/native RPC source from immutable bef1a565819c67f5403dd24ed6a35163a3a788eb under a newly admitted task without inheriting earlier proof.
- Bind public discovery, browser handoff, repository identity and expiry; preserve explicit entitlement/authority denials and uncertain mutation outcomes without replay. Caller retains private credential and pending-flow custody.
- Retain explicit SQLite, Neon and Supabase service APIs, optional feature combinations, Rust 1.75 and current-bearer native RPC.
- Configure ring and WebPKI roots per HTTPS client, preserving normal TLS verification without ambient provider effects or the unused HTTP/3 dependency graph. The independently reviewed lock removes 17 unused packages without dependency upgrades or replacements.
- Adopt a reviewed repository-local native proof contract and match the CI controller to the release-bound entrypoints.

## Evidence

This PR is created only by the released native workspace publisher after its complete workbranch boundary on candidate {{HEAD_SHA}} against accepted main {{BASE_SHA}}. Configured local proof covers formatting, all features, seven other feature combinations, clippy with warnings denied, specific missing-real-fixture failure, Rust 1.75, clean consumer resolution and package verification. Hosted controller CI, Pages and release remain explicit separate execution scopes.

## Remaining boundary

Loopback tests establish client transport behavior. No hosted PostgreSQL, managed Auth, seat/payment policy, deployment or registry publication is asserted. This ordinary library PR retains package version 0.11.1. Decapod #1628 remains blocked on the subsequent released Dactyl dependency; no downstream registry check or package handoff is weakened.

Closes #100.

spec_additions..decapod/managed/specs/ARCHITECTURE.md:
## Private HTTPS configuration boundary (issue 100)

`src/http_tls.rs` is a private module shared by the existing Neon, Supabase service/RPC and managed-auth transports, compiled only with an HTTP adapter feature. It builds an explicit rustls client configuration and passes it to reqwest through `use_preconfigured_tls`. The transport constructors retain their existing route, request and response contracts; the helper does not introduce a public adapter or session API. Client configuration errors propagate through `DactylError`.

Reqwest uses its WebPKI-roots feature without an implicit crypto provider. Dactyl explicitly selects ring and the same WebPKI root set per client, without enabling HTTP/3 or relying on the unused optional Quinn resolution edge. This preserves the supported Rust 1.75 consumer contract without activating an obsolete QUIC dependency. The generated lock and all-features dependency metadata must be reviewed, then the existing minimum-Rust, clean-consumer, feature and package checks must run against the admitted source. Dependency preparation alone is not a build or proof result.
spec_additions..decapod/managed/specs/SECURITY.md:
## Per-client TLS provider invariant (issue 100)

Every HTTPS adapter constructs its own ring provider and WebPKI trust store through `src/http_tls.rs`. The helper uses rustls safe default protocol versions, normal certificate and hostname verification, SNI and no client certificate. It neither installs nor reads a process-global crypto provider. An application's ambient provider cannot silently alter this connector's crypto policy, and Dactyl's client construction cannot change the application's provider. The repair does not add a custom verifier, insecure certificate option or HTTP/3 transport.

The isolated child-process regression must verify successful client construction with no ambient provider, absence of global installation as a side effect, and successful construction with an unrelated unusable ambient provider. It checks the configured TLS 1.2/1.3 cipher-suite policy and enabled SNI. Existing loopback transport fixtures remain required to catch a mismatched preconfigured TLS type. These checks establish configuration and client-construction behavior; they do not claim hosted TLS, managed Auth, account policy or deployment acceptance.
